sector: An independent prestige used vehicle dealership selling to retail buyers and part exchange customers from a single forecourt.
founded_place_size: Established 2006, one forecourt in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. A small independent holding about fourteen cars at a time, buying selectively rather than to volume.
about: Vanguard holds around fourteen carefully bought cars at a time and sells to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are choosing where to buy it. The card in the windscreen is the first thing a buyer meets, before anyone walks out, so it has to answer their two questions honestly: what is this car, and what does it cost.
audience: Private retail buyers aged 35 to 60 who have narrowed the choice online, driven a distance to see one specific car, and are deciding whether this dealer is careful.
price_positioning: Independent prestige used. Cars from 18,000 pounds to 95,000. Photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short spec of what differs between examples, the price plainly set and the finance line legible but secondary. Never the budget lot register, never a manufacturer brochure with no price.

palette.name: Midnight
palette.usage: The ground filling every card, as on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf, and the only ground or panel colour. Never a type colour.

palette.name: Vanguard Steel
palette.usage: Hairline rules and keylines only, such as the rule under the headline on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, panel or type colour.

palette.name: Chrome Silver
palette.usage: The shield, reproduced in pale ink on Midnight as on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf, and secondary type on Midnight such as the year, the model line, the name lockup, the spec block, the stock number or the registration. Never a ground, panel or the price.

palette.name: Brushed Pewter
palette.usage: The line carrying the mileage, transmission and fuel, and the finance footer with its monthly figure, as on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, panel, the price or display type.

palette.name: Signal White
palette.usage: The price, as on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf, and display or spec type on Midnight such as the stacked VANGUARD MOTORS name, the model line, the spec block, the stock number or the registration. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Marque Red
palette.usage: A thin rule or small mark only. Never a ground, panel or type colour, and never on the price, which the type system says is never coloured.

typography: Vanguard Motors runs two faces across four steps. Step 01 is the stacked marque in Righteous Regular 400 caps, VANGUARD at 42 pt on 46 pt tracked 0.18 em with MOTORS beneath at exactly one third the size, 14 pt, tracked 0.42 em so both lines measure the same width; on screen the marque sets at 64 px and the two lines are never set as one. Step 02 is the model line in Righteous Regular 400 at 34 pt on 38 pt, tracking -0.01 em. Step 03 is the spec in Suisse Int'l Regular at 11 pt on 15 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line, with the price in the same family at Medium 48 pt tabular lining and the mileage at 10 pt. Step 04 is the finance footer in Suisse Int'l Regular at 7.5 pt on 10 pt tracked 0.02 em, legible but secondary to the price.
voice: Factual, unhurried and confident, a dealer who lets the car and the spec do the talking. No exclamation, no urgency. Example: One owner, full history, the colour it says on the card and the colour it is on the forecourt.
brand_assets_status: The shield artwork is long gone. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door, weathered by several winters, carrying the shield at about 180mm. The current stock, specs and prices arrive from the stock feed, and the finance wording is fixed by the broker.
values: Cars bought with care and sold without spin, and a forecourt where the card and the vehicle always agree.

type_system.signature_move: The name always stacks on two lines, VANGUARD over MOTORS at exactly one third the size, with the tracking fitted on each line, 0.18 em on VANGUARD and 0.42 em on MOTORS, so both lines measure the same width. The two lines are never set as one.
rules: Never set the two lines as one: VANGUARD always stacks over MOTORS.
MOTORS is always exactly one third the size of VANGUARD.
Tracking is fitted per line so both lines measure the same width: 0.18 em on VANGUARD, 0.42 em on MOTORS.
On screen the marque sets at 64 px.
The price is plainly set in Suisse Int'l Medium 48 pt tabular lining, never styled up beyond Medium and never coloured.
The finance line is legible but always secondary to the price, and the broker's wording is set verbatim.
Never the budget lot register and never a manufacturer brochure with no price: the price is always present on the card.
One large honest photograph of the actual car leads the card; the type sits under it, quiet and plain.

palette_rules.distribution: Midnight fills every card and is the only ground or panel colour, as on windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf. On Midnight, the price is Signal White and the shield is Chrome Silver, as there; the line carrying the mileage, transmission and fuel, and the finance footer with its monthly figure, are Brushed Pewter, as there; every other line of type, the stacked VANGUARD MOTORS name, the year, the model line, the spec block, the stock number and the registration, is Signal White or Chrome Silver. Vanguard Steel and Marque Red are for hairline rules, keylines and small marks only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the car photograph: the type sits on solid Midnight beneath it.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons. No chrome, brushed-metal, foil, gradient or shine effect: Chrome Silver and Brushed Pewter are flat colours. No colour on the price but Signal White, and no price burst, starburst, flash or sale badge, the budget lot register the type system rules out.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs are not recoloured toward the palette: they are never tinted or graded toward Midnight or any other palette colour, and a silver car is not recoloured toward Chrome Silver nor a white one toward Signal White. A highlight clipped to white stays as shot: no palette colour, texture or panel detail is painted into it.
